Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Survey of Autonomous Agent Architectures

Alice Smith1, Bob Johnson2, Carol Williams3

1 Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA
2 Google DeepMind, London, UK
3 Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA

Abstract
Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled the development of
autonomous AI agents capable of complex reasoning, planning, and tool use. In this
survey, we provide a comprehensive overview of agentic AI systems, covering their
architecture, capabilities, and applications. We review over 200 papers published
between 2023 and 2025, categorizing agent designs into reactive, deliberative, and
hybrid architectures. Our analysis reveals key trends including the emergence of
multi-agent collaboration frameworks, improved grounding through tool integration,
and novel approaches to long-horizon planning. We also discuss open challenges
including safety, alignment, and evaluation methodology.

Keywords: autonomous agents, LLM agents, multi-agent systems, tool use, planning

1 Introduction

The field of artificial intelligence has witnessed a paradigm shift with the advent of
large language models capable of sophisticated reasoning and generation.
